title: Republic of Baja California
capsule: The Republic of Baja California was a filibuster state proclaimed on 3 November 1853 when the American adventurer William Walker landed at La Paz with roughly forty-five men and declared independence from Mexico, styling himself president. Walker later extended his proclaimed domain to a 'Republic of Sonora,' crossing into the mainland; however, sustained Mexican resistance, civilian hostility, and the desertion of most of his followers forced retreat. By January 1854 Walker surrendered to U.S. authorities at San Diego; a San Francisco jury subsequently acquitted him of violating U.S. neutrality laws.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Effective control was limited to a few coastal landing points for a matter of months; the territorial extent in any cartographic sense reflects Walker's proclaimed claims rather than any administered area.
